Program: Federal False Claims Act (FCA) qui tam
Primary scope: False claims to U.S.; Medicare/Medicaid claims can qualify
Who may receive: A private person may sue in U.S. name; statute says person, not limited to employees
Public-data treatment: Public disclosures can bar substantially same allegations unless DOJ brings case or relator is original source; current original-source exception requires independent knowledge materially adding to public disclosure and pre-filing voluntary disclosure. Public analysis alone does not guarantee this.
Payment trigger and amount: Government recovery by judgment, settlement, or alternate remedy; 15 to 25% if government proceeds and 25 to 30% if it declines and relator recovers. Separate statutory proviso permits no more than 10% where court finds action based primarily on specified public disclosures other than relator-provided information; this percentage rule is distinct from public-disclosure-bar/original-source eligibility.
Timing: Sealed complaint; government initially has at least 60 days and can obtain extensions; recovery/timing unpredictable
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: No ordinary anonymous tip payout. Filing under seal and government disclosure; identity may become public later. Necessary expenses and reasonable attorney fees/costs available only as statute allows after recovery; U.S. does not advance relator expenses. A declined case can expose relator to defendant fees if clearly frivolous/vexatious/harassing.
Overlaps: Federal/state cases and DOJ whistleblower programs can overlap, but bars, first-to-file, public-disclosure, and nonduplication rules apply. Not safe to count on multiple awards.

Current status on 2026-10-25: Active initial three-year pilot launched October20,2026. Reported launch check announced, but completed payment not independently verified.
Primary scope: Federal health-care offenses/related health-benefit crimes and fraud against patients/others in health industry; listed federal benefits programs; focus hospice, home health, day care, special services/autism fraud
Who may receive: Individual only; entities excluded; not meaningfully involved in crime (with narrow DOJ minimal-role exception); must cooperate
Public-data treatment: Independent public-data analysis can qualify if it reveals original nonpublic information previously unknown to DOJ and materially adds. Rules have unresolved tension over existing investigations and overlapping professional-source exclusions.
Payment trigger and amount: Unsealed indictment, information, or criminal complaint (unless DOJ chooses earlier); discretionary $10,000 to $30,000 per distinct tip; no minimum loss/forfeiture; may pay multiple eligible tipsters
Timing: DOJ says at or around criminal charge filing; not guaranteed; no reward while charge remains sealed unless DOJ chooses otherwise
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: No lawyer for named reports. Attorney required for anonymous submissions. Identity verified before payment. Cooperation can include records, testimony and proactive supervised work. DOJ may deny an award solely for reporting outside its portal. Current first form step:2000characters,5attachments,50MB each.
Overlaps: DOJ states WHIP does not preclude later award under other programs, including CWA.

Program: DOJ Criminal Division Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot (CWA)
Current status on 2026-10-25: Active three-year pilot effective 2024-08-01; scheduled for review after 3 years
Primary scope: Company-related federal health offenses and related crimes; fraud against patients, investors, or other non-governmental entities in healthcare industry; other enumerated corporate misconduct areas
Who may receive: Individual only; original info, voluntary submission, cooperation; culpability and other exclusions; no award to entity
Public-data treatment: Independent analysis of public sources is allowed if own analysis reveals information not generally known/available; information must be nonpublic, previously unknown to DOJ, and materially add to what DOJ has if DOJ has information.
Payment trigger and amount: Successful final forfeiture with >$1m net proceeds deposited in Assets Forfeiture Fund. Discretionary: up to 30% of first $100m, up to 5% from $100m to $500m, none above $500m; aggregate cap across awardees follows formula. Presumption of maximum 30% of first $10m if award appropriate and no reduction factors.
Timing: Only after forfeiture; claim within 90 days after DOJ publishes successful forfeiture notice; potentially lengthy and uncertain
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Attorney not required for named report; anonymous report requires lawyer, identity must be verified/disclosed before payment. Identity protected subject to law/policy and litigation disclosure; may share with enforcement agencies. Award is discretionary and guidance says no enforceable rights.
Overlaps: 2026 revision permits eligibility despite another program; DOJ will not issue duplicative awards and may deny/reduce for overlapping awards.

Current status on 2026-10-25: Regulation in 2025 CFR compilation; verify amendments
Who may receive: Any person except listed government/law-enforcement employees and close family, officials acting in duty, people who illegally obtained data, and participants
Public-data treatment: Information must identify a specific person/entity and time period. No reward if subject already under review/investigation by CMS, contractors, OIG, DOJ, FBI, or any federal/state/local law enforcement when submitted.
Payment trigger and amount: Recovery of at least $100 Medicare funds; discretionary maximum is 10% of overpayments or $1,000, whichever is less; shared across qualified informants; only if reward not otherwise provided by law
Timing: After all Medicare overpayments, fines, and penalties collected; promptness depends on case circumstances
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Reward claim requires identifying/contact information; CMS keeps identity confidential except as law requires; no interest; not guaranteed.
Overlaps: CMS pays only if a reward is not otherwise provided by law, creating uncertainty about combining with FCA/other statutory awards.

Current status on 2026-10-25: Active federal program; IRS Publication 5251 revised Aug. 2026
Primary scope: Specific, credible, timely information about tax underpayments or violations of laws IRS administers, enforces, or investigates; healthcare fraud alone is not enough unless there is a separate tax-law violation (for example, provider tax evasion or tax-exempt organization misuse).
Who may receive: An individual whistleblower who provides contact information and personally signs Form 211 under penalty of perjury; government/Treasury personnel and other listed ineligible persons are excluded. No award claim can be anonymous.
Public-data treatment: IRS says awards based on public-source information may have a lower percentage. No public-data independent-analysis safe harbor or automatic entitlement was verified; the information must be specific, credible, timely and lead to proceeds collected.
Payment trigger and amount: Generally 15 to 30% of proceeds collected attributable to the information. Mandatory §7623(b) applies only where proceeds in dispute exceed $2 million and, if the subject is an individual taxpayer, the taxpayer had gross income over $200,000 in a year at issue. Below those thresholds IRS may consider a discretionary §7623(a) award; no guaranteed floor.
Timing: Submit Form 211 before IRS proceeds with an action based on the information (IRS Internal Revenue Manual); payment only after final tax determination, award determination, and appeals/waiver. Tax resolution and collection may take years.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Attorney not required for a named award claim; award applicant must identify themself, provide contact details, and sign personally under penalty of perjury. IRS protects identity to extent law allows; tax return information and investigation details are restricted, but this is not a promise of absolute anonymity. IRS does not promise reimbursement of source research costs.
Overlaps: This rewards tax-law enforcement proceeds, not the underlying healthcare billing loss as such. A healthcare matter could separately generate FCA/DOJ/CMS routes if their elements are met; do not assume same recovery can be counted twice or that tax and health-fraud awards are cumulative.

Current status on 2026-10-25: Active federal program; FY2025 SEC annual report available
Primary scope: Possible federal securities-law violation; healthcare fraud alone is not enough. Could be relevant only if the same conduct also involves a securities violation, such as materially false issuer disclosures or fraud in securities offerings.
Who may receive: Eligible individuals (not companies) who voluntarily provide original information in writing and satisfy the statutory/rule criteria. Anonymous tips may qualify for an award only when submitted through an attorney who certifies the submission; the whistleblower still personally signs the required Form TCR under penalty of perjury.
Public-data treatment: Independent analysis of public information can qualify if it reveals information not generally known and provides important insights not apparent on the face of the material; merely pointing SEC staff to public records and alleging fraud does not qualify. SEC must not already know the information.
Payment trigger and amount: 10 to 30% in aggregate of monetary sanctions collected in an SEC Covered Action with over $1 million in sanctions; certain related-action awards may also be available if the SEC award criteria are met. Award percentage is determined by the Commission.
Timing: Submit directly to SEC using its online TCR portal or Form TCR; qualifying information must be submitted in the required manner and timing. Apply for an award on Form WB-APP within 90 calendar days after the SEC posts a Notice of Covered Action. Awards follow successful enforcement and collections; timing may be years.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Attorney not required for a named tip; mandatory for anonymous award submissions. SEC promises confidentiality to the fullest extent possible but lists legal disclosure exceptions. Award claim itself is not anonymous to SEC; counsel fees/research costs are not guaranteed reimbursement.
Overlaps: No general healthcare-fraud bounty. A parallel SEC award is possible only for a distinct securities-law violation and a qualifying SEC enforcement/related action; do not presume duplicative awards or that an FCA/DOJ healthcare tip satisfies SEC rules.

Who may receive: Varies; confirm statutory definition, public-disclosure and first-to-file rules, procedural requirements, limitation periods and local law
Public-data treatment: State-specific. HHS-OIG Medicaid approval is not a complete law or eligibility census.

Program: California False Claims Act (CFCA), Cal. Gov. Code §§12650 to 12656
Current status on 2026-10-25: Active; HHS-OIG lists California approved 2019-01-25; official §12652 read through normal browser
Primary scope: False claims involving California/state or local public funds, including Medi-Cal
Who may receive: Private qui tam plaintiff; special restrictions apply to some public employees and public-disclosure cases
Public-data treatment: California public-disclosure/original-source rules apply independently; public allegations can bar case absent exception.
Payment trigger and amount: Successful recovery: 15 to 33% if state proceeds; 25 to 50% if state declines and relator wins/settles
Timing: Sealed complaint and state review; duration uncertain
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Identity may become public later; litigated case. Fee/cost reimbursement subject to statute and recovery; not upfront guaranteed.
Overlaps: Potential parallel federal FCA/Medi-Cal claims; coordinate due to first-to-file and public-disclosure rules.

Program: California Insurance Frauds Prevention Act (IFPA), Cal. Ins. Code §1871.7
Current status on 2026-10-25: Active; includes health insurance fraud under specified provisions
Primary scope: Specified insurance fraud, including private health insurance claims
Who may receive: An “interested person”; California appellate decisions say no personal injury is required, but statutory eligibility/public-disclosure rules still apply
Public-data treatment: Separate state public-disclosure/original-source bar; public-info opportunism can defeat suit. Must voluntarily disclose direct/independent source info to DA/Insurance Commissioner before filing where bar applies.
Payment trigger and amount: Successful civil case/recovery: generally 30 to 40% if DA/Commissioner proceeds; 40 to 50% if both decline and relator succeeds; statutory conditions apply
Timing: Complaint served on DA and Insurance Commissioner; 60-day intervention period, extensions possible
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Complex civil case, not an intake bounty. Attorney costs/fees may be recoverable if successful but terms/upfront funding not guaranteed. Relator identity may later be public. Official text read through normal browser on 2026-10-25 after automated access failed.
Overlaps: May overlap federal criminal/CWA/WHIP or FCA if a government plan is also implicated, subject-matter-specific rules apply.

Program: Illinois Insurance Claims Fraud Prevention Act (ICFPA), 740 ILCS 92
Primary scope: Enumerated fraud/kickback conduct involving private insurance claims
Who may receive: Statute requires an “interested person”; Illinois appellate court held patient with no direct injury and no involvement in billing was not eligible. Poor fit for pure public-data outsider absent qualifying involvement.
Public-data treatment: Statutory public-disclosure share reduction can cap at 10% absent relator-supplied information; other eligibility/pleading rules apply.
Payment trigger and amount: Successful recovery: at least 30% if government proceeds; at least 40% if it declines; a public-disclosure exception can permit up to 10%; subject to terms
Timing: State AG/prosecutor notice and intervention procedure; civil case timing uncertain
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Litigation; reasonable expenses and attorneys’ fees may be awarded against defendant on success; no advance from state; identity may be public.
Overlaps: Private insurer route distinct from Illinois False Claims Act for public funds. Avoid duplicate recovery assumptions.

Program: Private insurer SIU / state insurance fraud reporting
Current status on 2026-10-25: Reporting channels verified in sampled insurer pages; no general cash bounty advertised; see insurer-checks.csv
Primary scope: Suspected fraud against a private insurer or insured
Who may receive: Anyone may provide a lead; no bounty eligibility because typical route has no reward terms
Public-data treatment: May be useful lead; can be shared/investigated; not itself a qui tam case
Payment trigger and amount: No general bounty; tip-only unless a specific statute/program expressly applies (e.g., CA IFPA or IL ICFPA)
Timing: Agency/insurer decides whether to investigate; no report-to-payment timetable
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Often accepts reports; no attorney required for a tip, but no guaranteed anonymity or compensation.
Overlaps: DOJ WHIP/CWA may be relevant if program subject area and causation/forfeiture criteria fit; special state statutes may offer civil qui tam only to eligible relators.

Program: Arkansas Medicaid Fraud False Claims Act informant reward, Ark. Code §20-77-911
Current status on 2026-10-25: Active; 2025 code text consulted on secondary code host
Primary scope: False Medicaid claims under Arkansas Medicaid fraud false claims subchapter; award tied to civil-penalty recovery and detection/prosecution
Who may receive: Any person providing qualifying information; exclusions include government employees or contractors charged with referring/investigating Medicaid fraud
Public-data treatment: Statute does not state a public-data exclusion; court/AG assess whether information led to detection and trial/punishment. Public analysis alone does not establish eligibility.
Payment trigger and amount: Court may award up to 10% of aggregate collected civil penalties; current 2025 text has no dollar cap. No portion of restitution may be used. AG may petition after civil-penalty recovery or agree up to 10% of civil penalty in settlement; if AG declines to petition, person may petition court.
Timing: After civil penalty recovery or settlement/other disposition; no predictable timing or assured payment.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: This is a state statutory informant reward, not a general tip-line payment. Court/AG discretion; statute says state/defendant not liable for petitioner expenses. Legal review needed before relying on petition route.
Overlaps: Separate from Arkansas Medicaid FCA qui tam posture; coordinate and do not assume both awards can be collected for same matter.

Program: California Medi-Cal fraud information reward, Welf. & Inst. Code §14107.12
Current status on 2026-10-25: Statutory authority verified in current official code through normal browser; no operating payment process independently tested
Primary scope: Information leading to recovery of at least $100 in Medi-Cal public funds tied to conduct underlying a Medi-Cal provider conviction
Who may receive: Any person, subject to exclusions including officials/employees or contractors with information acquired through their assigned work
Public-data treatment: No public-source exclusion stated in the statute located; information must lead to recovery and meet subject/time-period requirements. Public analysis is not automatically qualifying.
Payment trigger and amount: Discretionary reward up to the lesser of 10% of restitution actually recovered or $1,000; paid only from recovered DOJ funds legally usable for rewards.
Timing: After provider conviction and only after all recoverable funds have been collected; no fixed payment timeline established.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Tip/reward rather than private qui tam litigation. Payment is discretionary and limited by available recovered funds; eligibility restrictions apply.
Overlaps: Potentially distinct from CFCA/DOJ criminal routes; statute does not establish duplicate awards. Do not count overlapping recoveries.

Program: Florida Medicaid fraud reporting reward, Fla. Stat. §409.9203
Primary scope: Criminal fraud upon Medicaid funds or criminal violation of Florida Medicaid laws by another person
Who may receive: A person furnishing original information and reporting to specified state entities; reward subject to available funds
Public-data treatment: No public-data exclusion stated, but information must be original, relate to criminal Medicaid fraud, be reported to a listed agency, and lead to recovery of a fine, penalty, or forfeiture. Public analysis is not automatically qualifying.
Payment trigger and amount: Mandatory subject to fund availability if statutory conditions met; maximum is the lesser of 25% of amount recovered or $500,000 per case. A recipient cannot also receive Florida FCA funds for the same Medicaid fraud.
Timing: After resulting fine/penalty/forfeiture recovery; no fixed date specified.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: This is a state information reward, not a general civil qui tam share. Reward depends on original information, qualifying report and recovery.
Overlaps: Express statutory bar prevents receiving Florida FCA funds for Medicaid fraud for which this reward is received; other overlap not resolved by this provision.

Program: Kansas public-treasury/Medicaid fraud informant reward, K.S.A. 75-727
Primary scope: Violations of Medicaid Fraud Control Act, False Claims Act, or other law protecting public treasury
Who may receive: Any person who first furnishes information; governmental employees excluded unless information unrelated to their responsibilities as determined by AG
Public-data treatment: No express public-data exclusion; AG must certify the information was previously unknown and materially contributed to its investigation.
Payment trigger and amount: Discretionary AG award not exceeding $5,000; only after judgment for state or conviction; paid from Medicaid fraud prosecution revolving fund.
Timing: Only after judgment or conviction; no standard payment time specified.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Sole AG discretion; statute gives no guarantee and may exclude government employees.
Overlaps: Could overlap state FCA or Medicaid criminal enforcement; no duplicate-award rule verified.

Program: Texas Medicaid fraud/abuse/overcharge reporting award, Tex. Gov’t Code §544.0205
Primary scope: Medicaid fraud, abuse, or overcharges resulting in recovery of a remedy under Tex. Hum. Res. Code §32.039
Who may receive: Individual; not an entity. Award unavailable if commission or AG had independent knowledge.
Public-data treatment: No public-data exclusion stated; however agency/AG must lack independent knowledge and report disclosure must result in a statutory recovery. Public information alone does not guarantee eligibility.
Payment trigger and amount: Discretionary award up to 5% of the qualifying §32.039 remedy; agency considers fiscal importance and may consider degree of participation. A person bringing an action under the Medicaid FCA is ineligible for this award.
Timing: After the report results in recovered remedy; no fixed payment timing stated.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: Statute says commission may grant award; no entitlement or cost reimbursement promise verified.
Overlaps: Expressly excludes person who brings action under Tex. Hum. Res. Code ch.36 Medicaid FCA for the same reporting award.

Program: Louisiana Medical Assistance Programs tip reward, La. R.S. 46:440.2 / LAC 50:I.4605
Current status on 2026-10-25: Statute and current promulgated rule verified. Funding and actual payment history not established.
Primary scope: Information about fraud/abuse under the Louisiana Medicaid Medical Assistance Program Integrity Law that results in a recovery
Who may receive: Qualifying information supplier. Rule excludes previously known information, participants, certain Medicaid-excluded or recovery-subject people and public-duty reporters.
Public-data treatment: Information must result in recovery. Previously known information is excluded. No automatic eligibility for independent public analysis.
Payment trigger and amount: Secretary may approve up to $2,000 for information resulting in recovery, only from appropriated funds. Discretionary.
Timing: After recovery; no fixed timing stated.
Attorney/confidentiality/cost notes: No private lawsuit required. Current sections 4605 and 4607 govern award and exclusions. Funding and payment practice remain unverified.
Overlaps: Separate from Louisiana Medicaid FCA qui tam share; no cumulative payment assumption.
